arxiv-1705-10588.title: An Overview of Recent Progress in Laser Wakefield Acceleration Experiments
arxiv-1705-10588.creator: S.P.D. Mangles
arxiv-1705-10588.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by S.P.D. Mangles. The goal of this paper is to examine experimental progress in laser wakefield acceleration over the past decade (2004–2014), and to use trends in the data to understand some of the important physical processes. By examining a set of over 50 experiments, various trends concerning the relationship between plasma density, accelerator length, laser power and the final electron beam energy are revealed.

arxiv-2302-14722.title: Quasinormal modes of a holonomy corrected Schwarzschild black hole
arxiv-2302-14722.creator: Zeus S. Moreira, Haroldo C. D. Lima Junior, Luís C. B. Crispino, Carlos A. R. Herdeiro
arxiv-2302-14722.description: Abstract We analyze the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a recently obtained solution of a Schwarzschild black hole (BH) with corrections motivated by Loop Quantum Gravity (LQG). This spacetime is regular everywhere and presents the global structure of a wormhole, with a minimal surface whose radius depends on a LQG parameter.

arxiv-2411-09936.description: Abstract Deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) has shown promise in wireless transmission of text, speech, and images within the realm of semantic communication. arxiv-2502-07544.title: Grammar Control in Dialogue Response Generation for Language Learning Chatbots
arxiv-2502-07544.creator: Dominik Glandorf, Peng Cui, Detmar Meurers, Mrinmaya Sachan
arxiv-2502-07544.description: Abstract Chatbots based on large language models offer cheap conversation practice opportunities for language learners. However, they are hard to control for linguistic forms that correspond to learners’ current needs, such as grammar. We control grammar in chatbot conversation practice by grounding a dialogue response generation model in a pedagogical repository of grammar skills.
